arabic_blocks: [1180] حدثنا موسى بن إسماعيل حدثنا مهدي بن ميمون حدثنا واصل الأحدب عن المعرور بن سويد عن أبي ذر رضى الله تعالى عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: أتاني آت من ربي فأخبرني أو قال بشرني أنه من مات من أمتي لا يشرك بالله شيئا دخل الجنة قلت: وإن زنى وإن سرق قال وإن زنى وإن سرق
english_blocks: Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. Mahdi ibn Maymun related to us. Wasil al-Ahdab related to us, from al-Ma‘rur ibn Suwayd, from Abu Dharr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Someone came to me from my Lord and informed me—or he said, gave me good news—that whoever of my community dies without associating anything with Allah will enter Paradise.” I said, “Even if he has committed unlawful sexual intercourse, and even if he has stolen?” He said, “Even if he has committed unlawful sexual intercourse, and even if he has stolen.”

arabic_blocks: [1181] حدثنا عمر بن حفص حدثنا أبي حدثنا الأعمش حدثنا شقيق عن عبد الله رضى الله تعالى عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: من مات يشرك بالله شيئا دخل النار وقلت: أنا من مات لا يشرك بالله شيئا دخل الجنة
english_blocks: ‘Umar ibn Hafs related to us. My father related to us. Al-A‘mash related to us. Shaqiq related to us, from ‘Abdullah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:
“Whoever dies associating anything with Allah will enter the Fire.”
And I said: “Whoever dies without associating anything with Allah will enter Paradise.”

arabic_blocks: [1182] حدثنا أبو الوليد حدثنا شعبة عن الأشعث قال: سمعت معاوية بن سويد بن مقرن عن البراء رضى الله تعالى عنه قال أمرنا النبي ﷺ بسبع ونهانا عن سبع أمرنا باتباع الجنائز وعيادة المريض وإجابة الداعي ونصر المظلوم وإبرار القسم ورد السلام وتشميت العاطس ونهانا عن آنية الفضة وخاتم الذهب والحرير والديباج والقسي والإستبرق
english_blocks: Abu al-Walid related to us. Shu‘bah related to us, from al-Ash‘ath, who said: I heard Mu‘awiyah ibn Suwayd ibn Muqarrin, from al-Bara’, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, instructed us to do seven things and forbade us seven. He instructed us to follow funeral processions, visit the sick, answer an invitation, support the wronged, fulfil an oath, return the greeting of peace and invoke blessings on one who sneezes. He forbade us silver vessels, a gold ring, silk, brocade, qassi cloth and thick brocade.

arabic_blocks: [1183] حدثنا محمد حدثنا عمرو بن أبي سلمة عن الأوزاعي قال: أخبرني ابن شهاب قال: أخبرني سعيد بن المسيب أن أبا هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه قال: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول: حق المسلم على المسلم خمس رد السلام وعيادة المريض واتباع الجنائز وإجابة الدعوة وتشميت العاطس تابعه عبد الرزاق قال: أخبرنا معمر ، ورواه سلامة عن عقيل
english_blocks: Muhammad related to us. ‘Amr ibn Abi Salamah related to us, from al-Awza‘i, who said: Ibn Shihab informed me. He said: Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab informed me that Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say:
“The rights of a Muslim over a Muslim are five: returning the greeting of peace, visiting the sick, following funeral processions, answering an invitation and invoking blessings on one who sneezes.”
‘Abd al-Razzaq corroborated it. He said: Ma‘mar informed us. Salamah also related it from ‘Uqayl.

arabic_blocks: [1184] حدثنا بشر بن محمد أخبرنا عبد الله قال: أخبرني معمر ويونس عن الزهري قال: أخبرني أبو سلمة أن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها زوج النبي ﷺ أخبرته قالت أقبل أبو بكر رضى الله تعالى عنه على فرسه من مسكنه بالسنح حتى نزل فدخل المسجد فلم يكلم الناس حتى دخل على عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها فتيمم النبي ﷺ وهو مسجى ببرد حبرة فكشف عن وجهه ثم أكب عليه فقبله ثم بكى، فقال بأبي أنت يا نبي الله لا يجمع الله عليك موتتين أما الموتة التي كتبت عليك فقدمتها
english_blocks: Bishr ibn Muhammad related to us. ‘Abdullah informed us. He said: Ma‘mar and Yunus informed me, from al-Zuhri, who said: Abu Salamah informed me that ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, informed him. She said:

Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, came on his horse from his dwelling at al-Sunh. He dismounted and entered the mosque, and did not speak to the people until he went in to ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her. He went towards the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who was covered with a striped cloak. He uncovered his face, then bent over him and kissed him, then wept. He said, “May my father be your ransom, O Prophet of Allah. Allah will not bring two deaths upon you. As for the death that was decreed for you, you have died it.”

arabic_blocks: [1185] قال أبو سلمة فأخبرني ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما أن أبا بكر رضى الله تعالى عنه خرج وعمر رضى الله تعالى عنه يكلم الناس، فقال اجلس فأبى، فقال اجلس فأبى فتشهد أبو بكر رضى الله تعالى عنه فمال إليه الناس وتركوا عمر، فقال: أما بعد فمن كان منكم يعبد محمدا ﷺ فإن محمدا ﷺ قد مات ومن كان يعبد الله فإن الله حي لا يموت قال الله تعالى { وما محمد إلا رسول } إلى { الشاكرين } والله لكأن الناس لم يكونوا يعلمون أن الله أنزلها حتى تلاها أبو بكر رضى الله تعالى عنه فتلقاها منه الناس فما يسمع بشر إلا يتلوها
english_blocks: Abu Salamah said: Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, informed me:

Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, went out while ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, was speaking to the people. He said, “Sit down,” but he refused. He said, “Sit down,” but he refused. Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, then pronounced the testimony of faith. The people turned towards him and left ‘Umar. He said, “To proceed: whoever among you used to worship Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, has died. Whoever used to worship Allah, Allah is living and does not die. Allah Most High said: ‘And Muhammad is only a messenger,’ up to ‘the thankful.’”

By Allah, it was as though the people had not known that Allah had revealed it until Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, recited it. The people received it from him, and no one was heard but that he was reciting it.

arabic_blocks: [1186] حدثنا يحيى بن بكير حدثنا الليث عن عقيل عن ابن شهاب قال: أخبرني خارجة بن زيد بن ثابت أن أم العلاء امرأة من الأنصار بايعت النبي ﷺ أخبرته أنه اقتسم المهاجرون قرعة فطار لنا عثمان بن مظعون فأنزلناه في أبياتنا فوجع وجعه الذي توفي فيه فلما توفي وغسل وكفن في أثوابه دخل رسول الله ﷺ فقلت: رحمة الله عليك أبا السائب فشهادتي عليك لقد أكرمك الله، فقال النبي ﷺ وما يدريك أن الله أكرمه فقلت: بأبي أنت يا رسول الله فمن يكرمه الله، فقال: أما هو فقد جاءه اليقين والله إني لأرجو له الخير والله ما أدري وأنا رسول الله ما يفعل بي قالت فوالله لا أزكي أحدا بعده أبدا حدثنا سعيد بن عفير حدثنا الليث مثله، وقال نافع بن يزيد عن عقيل ما يفعل به وتابعه شعيب وعمرو بن دينار ومعمر
english_blocks: Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. Al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Kharijah ibn Zayd ibn Thabit informed me that Umm al-‘Ala’, a woman of the Ansar who had pledged allegiance to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, informed him:

The Emigrants were allotted by drawing lots, and ‘Uthman ibn Maz‘un fell to our lot. We lodged him in our rooms. He then suffered the illness in which he died. When he had died, been washed and been shrouded in his clothes, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered. I said, “Allah’s mercy be upon you, Abu al-Sa’ib. I bear witness concerning you that Allah has indeed honoured you.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “How do you know that Allah has honoured him?” I said, “May my father be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah. Whom, then, will Allah honour?”

He said, “As for him, certainty has come to him. By Allah, I do hope for good for him. By Allah, I do not know, though I am the Messenger of Allah, what will be done with me.” She said, “By Allah, I will never vouch for anyone after him, ever.”
Sa‘id ibn ‘Ufayr related to us. Al-Layth related to us the like of it. Nafi‘ ibn Yazid said, from ‘Uqayl: “What will be done with him.” Shu‘ayb, ‘Amr ibn Dinar and Ma‘mar corroborated it.

arabic_blocks: [1187] حدثنا محمد بن بشار حدثنا غندر حدثنا شعبة قال: سمعت محمد بن المنكدر قال: سمعت جابر بن عبد الله رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال لما قتل أبي جعلت أكشف الثوب عن وجهه أبكى وينهونني عنه والنبي ﷺ لا ينهاني فجعلت عمتي فاطمة تبكي، فقال النبي ﷺ تبكين أو لا تبكين ما زالت الملائكة تظله بأجنحتها حتى رفعتموه تابعه بن جريج أخبرني ابن المنكدر سمع جابرا رضى الله تعالى عنه
english_blocks: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. Ghundar related to us. Shu‘bah related to us. He said: I heard Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir say: I heard Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, say:

When my father was killed, I began uncovering the cloth from his face, weeping, and they were forbidding me from doing so, but the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not forbid me. My aunt Fatimah began weeping. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Whether you weep or do not weep, the angels continued shading him with their wings until you lifted him.”
Ibn Jurayj corroborated it: Ibn al-Munkadir informed me that he heard Jabir, may Allah Most High be pleased with him.

english_blocks: Muhammad related to us. Abu Mu‘awiyah informed us, from Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani, from al-Sha‘bi, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

A person whom the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to visit died. He died at night, and they buried him at night. In the morning they informed him. He said, “What prevented you from letting me know?” They said, “It was night—and dark—and we disliked causing you hardship.” So he went to his grave and prayed over him.

english_blocks: Muslim related to us. Shu‘bah related to us. ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Asbahani related to us, from Dhakwan, from Abu Sa‘id, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

The women said to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “Set aside a day for us.” He exhorted them and said, “Any woman whose three children die, they will be a barrier for her from the Fire.” A woman said, “And two?” He said, “And two.”

Sharik said, from Ibn al-Asbahani: Abu Salih related to me, from Abu Sa‘id and Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Abu Hurayrah said: “They had not reached puberty.”

english_blocks: Isma‘il ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Umm ‘Atiyyah al-Ansariyyah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came in to us when his daughter died. He said, “Wash her three or five times, or more than that if you see fit, with water and lote leaves. Put camphor—or some camphor—in the last washing. When you have finished, let me know.” When we had finished, we let him know. He gave us his waist-wrapper and said, “Place it next to her body.”

english_blocks: Muhammad related to us. ‘Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi related to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, from Umm ‘Atiyyah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came in to us while we were washing his daughter. He said, “Wash her three or five times, or more than that, with water and lote leaves. Put camphor in the last washing. When you have finished, let me know.” When we had finished, we let him know. He cast his waist-wrapper to us and said, “Place it next to her body.”

Ayyub said: Hafsah also related to me the like of Muhammad’s hadith. Hafsah’s hadith included: “Wash her an odd number of times.” It included: “Three or five or seven.” It included that he said: “Begin with her right side and her places of ablution.” It included that Umm ‘Atiyyah said: “We combed her hair into three braids.”

english_blocks: Hamid ibn ‘Umar related to us. Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, from Umm ‘Atiyyah, who said:

One of the daughters of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, died. He came out and said, “Wash her three or five times, or more than that if you see fit, with water and lote leaves. Put camphor—or some camphor—in the last washing. When you have finished, let me know.” She said: When we had finished, we let him know. He cast his waist-wrapper to us and said, “Place it next to her body.”

And from Ayyub, from Hafsah, from Umm ‘Atiyyah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, the like of it. She said that he said: “Wash her three or five or seven times, or more than that if you see fit.” Hafsah said: Umm ‘Atiyyah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, said: “We arranged the hair on her head into three braids.”

arabic_blocks: [1202] حدثنا أحمد حدثنا عبد الله بن وهب أخبرنا ابن جريج أن أيوب أخبره قال: سمعت ابن سيرين يقول جاءت أم عطية رضى الله تعالى عنها امرأة من الأنصار من اللاتي بايعن قدمت البصرة تبادر ابنا لها فلم تدركه فحدثتنا قالت دخل علينا النبي ﷺ ونحن نغسل ابنته، فقال اغسلنها ثلاثا أو خمسا أو أكثر من ذلك إن رأيتن ذلك بماء وسدر واجعلن في الآخرة كافورا فإذا فرغتن فآذنني قالت فلما فرغنا ألقى إلينا حقوه، فقال أشعرنها إياه ولم يزد على ذلك ولا أدري أي بناته وزعم أن الإشعار الففنها فيه وكذلك كان ابن سرين يأمر بالمرأة أن تشعر ولا تؤزر
english_blocks: Ahmad related to us. ‘Abdullah ibn Wahb related to us. Ibn Jurayj informed us that Ayyub informed him. He said: I heard Ibn Sirin say:

Umm ‘Atiyyah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, came—a woman of the Ansar, one of those who had pledged allegiance. She came to Basra, hastening to reach a son of hers, but she did not reach him. She related to us, saying:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came in to us while we were washing his daughter. He said, “Wash her three or five times, or more than that if you see fit, with water and lote leaves. Put camphor in the last washing. When you have finished, let me know.” She said: When we had finished, he cast his waist-wrapper to us and said, “Place it next to her body.”

He did not add anything beyond that. I do not know which of his daughters it was. And he stated that ishar means: “Wrap her in it.” Likewise, Ibn Sirin used to instruct that a woman be wrapped in it, not have it tied around her waist.

arabic_blocks: [1203] حدثنا قبيصة حدثنا سفيان عن هشام عن أم الهذيل عن أم عطية رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت ضفرنا شعر بنت النبي ﷺ تعني ثلاثة قرون، وقال وكيع قال سفيان ناصيتها وقرنيها
english_blocks: Qabisah related to us. Sufyan related to us, from Hisham, from Umm al-Hudhayl, from Umm ‘Atiyyah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:
We braided the hair of the daughter of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.
She means three braids.
Waki‘ said: Sufyan said: “Her forelock and her two side locks.”

arabic_blocks: [1204] حدثنا مسدد حدثنا يحيى بن سعيد عن هشام بن حسان قال: حدثتنا حفصة عن أم عطية رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت توفيت إحدى بنات النبي ﷺ فأتانا النبي ﷺ، فقال اغسلنها بالسدر وترا ثلاثا أو خمسا أو أكثر من ذلك إن رأيتن ذلك واجعلن في الآخرة كافورا أو شيئا من كافور فإذا فرغتن فآذنني فلما فرغنا آذناه فألقى إلينا حقوه فضفرنا شعرها ثلاثة قرون وألقيناها خلفها
english_blocks: Musaddad related to us. Yahya ibn Sa‘id related to us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, who said: Hafsah related to us, from Umm ‘Atiyyah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

One of the daughters of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, died. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to us and said, “Wash her with lote leaves an odd number of times—three or five, or more than that if you see fit. Put camphor—or some camphor—in the last washing. When you have finished, let me know.” When we had finished, we let him know. He cast his waist-wrapper to us. We braided her hair into three braids and placed them behind her.

english_blocks: Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. Hammad related to us, from Ayyub, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them, who said:

While a man was standing at ‘Arafah, he fell from his mount and it broke his neck—or he said, caused his neck to break. Do not apply burial perfume to him, and do not cover his head, for he will be raised on the Day of Resurrection reciting the talbiyah.”

english_blocks: Qutaybah related to us. Hammad related to us, from Ayyub, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

Do not apply burial perfume to him, and do not cover his head, for Allah will raise him on the Day of Resurrection reciting the talbiyah.”

english_blocks: Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. Abu ‘Awanah informed us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them:

A man’s camel broke his neck while we were with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he was in ihram. Do not touch him with perfume, and do not cover his head, for Allah will raise him on the Day of Resurrection reciting the talbiyah.”

arabic_blocks: [1209] حدثنا مسدد حدثنا حماد بن زيد عن عمرو وأيوب عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهم قال: كان رجل واقف مع النبي ﷺ بعرفة فوقع عن راحلته قال أيوب فوقصته، وقال عمرو فأقصعته فمات، فقال اغسلوه بماء وسدر وكفنوه في ثوبين ولا تحنطوه ولا تخمروا رأسه فإنه يبعث يوم القيامة قال أيوب يلبي، وقال عمرو ملبيا
english_blocks: Musaddad related to us. Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from ‘Amr and Ayyub, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them, who said:
A man was standing with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, at ‘Arafah, and he fell from his mount.
Ayyub said: “It broke his neck.” ‘Amr said: “It crushed him.”
He died. He said, “Wash him with water and lote leaves, and shroud him in two cloths. Do not apply burial perfume to him, and do not cover his head, for he will be raised on the Day of Resurrection.”
Ayyub said: “He recites the talbiyah.” ‘Amr said: “Reciting the talbiyah.”

arabic_blocks: [1210] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى بن سعيد عن عبيد الله قال: حدثني نافع عن ابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما أن عبد الله بن أبي لما توفي جاء ابنه إلى النبي ﷺ، فقال: يا رسول الله أعطني قميصك أكفنه فيه وصل عليه واستغفر له فأعطاه النبي ﷺ قميصه، فقال آذني أصلي عليه فآذنه فلما أراد أن يصلي عليه جذبه عمر رضى الله تعالى عنه، فقال أليس الله نهاك أن تصلي على المنافقين، فقال: أنا بين خيرتين قال { استغفر لهم أو لا تستغفر لهم إن تستغفر لهم سبعين مرة فلن يغفر الله لهم } فصلى عليه فنزلت { ولا تصل على أحد منهم مات أبدا }
english_blocks: Musaddad related to us; he said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id related to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah, who said: Nafi‘ related to me, from Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both:

When ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy died, his son came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, “Messenger of Allah, give me your shirt so that I may shroud him in it, pray over him, and ask forgiveness for him.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gave him his shirt and said, “Let me know, so that I may pray over him.” He let him know. When he was about to pray over him, ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, pulled him and said, “Has Allah not forbidden you to pray over the hypocrites?” He said, “I am between two choices. He said: ‘Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them. If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will never forgive them.’” He prayed over him, and then it was revealed: “And never pray over any of them who dies.”

english_blocks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Makki related to us: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us, from Sa‘d, from his father, who said:

‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, was brought his food one day. He said, “Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr was killed, and he was better than I. Nothing was found in which to shroud him except a burdah. Hamzah—or another man better than I—was killed, and nothing was found in which to shroud him except a burdah. I have indeed feared that our good things may have been hastened for us in our worldly life.” Then he began to weep.

“And Hamzah was killed, and he was better than I. Then this world was opened up to us as it was opened up”—

“We were given of this world what we were given. And we have feared that our good deeds have been hastened for us.” Then he began to weep until he left the food.

We emigrated with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, seeking the Face of Allah, so our reward became due from Allah. Some of us died without eating anything of their reward; among them was Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr. And among us is one whose fruit has ripened, and he is plucking it. He was killed on the day of Uhud, and we found nothing in which to shroud him except a burdah. When we covered his head with it, his feet showed, and when we covered his feet, his head showed. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, commanded us to cover his head and to put some idhkhir on his feet.

english_blocks: ‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah related to us: Ibn Abi Hazim related to us, from his father, from Sahl, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:
A woman came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with a woven burdah with its border.
“Do you know what a burdah is?” They said, “A wrap.” He said, “Yes.”

She said, “I wove it with my hand and have come to clothe you in it.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, took it, being in need of it. He came out to us wearing it as his waist-wrapper. So-and-so admired it and said, “Clothe me in it. How beautiful it is!” The people said, “You have not done well. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wore it because he needed it, and then you asked him for it, knowing that he does not refuse.” He said, “By Allah, I did not ask him for it to wear it. I only asked him for it so that it would be my shroud.”
Sahl said: It became his shroud.

english_blocks: Adam related to us: Shu‘bah related to us: Thabit related to us, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed a woman weeping at a grave. He said, “Fear Allah and be patient.” She said, “Away from me, for you have not been afflicted with my calamity.” She did not recognize him. She was told, “He is the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.” She came to the door of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and found no doorkeepers there. She said, “I did not recognize you.” He said, “Patience is only at the first shock.”

arabic_blocks: [1224] حدثنا عبدان ومحمد قالا: أخبرنا عبد الله أخبرنا عاصم بن سليمان عن أبي عثمان قال: حدثني أسامة بن زيد رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال أرسلت ابنة النبي ﷺ إليه إن ابنا لي قبض فائتنا فأرسل يقريء السلام ويقول إن لله ما أخذ وله ما أعطى وكل عنده بأجل مسمى فلتصبر ولتحتسب فأرسلت إليه تقسم عليه ليأتينها فقام ومعه سعد بن عبادة ومعاذ بن جبل وأبي بن كعب وزيد بن ثابت ورجال فرفع إلى رسول الله ﷺ الصبي ونفسه تتقعقع قال حسبته أنه قال: كانها شن ففاضت عيناه، فقال سعد يا رسول الله ما هذا، فقال هذه رحمة جعلها الله في قلوب عباده وإنما يرحم الله من عباده الرحماء
english_blocks: ‘Abdan and Muhammad related to us; they said: ‘Abd Allah informed us: ‘Asim ibn Sulayman informed us, from Abu ‘Uthman, who said: Usamah ibn Zayd, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, related to me; he said:

The daughter of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent to him: “A son of mine is dying, so come to us.” He sent greetings of peace and said, “To Allah belongs what He takes, and to Him belongs what He gives. Everything with Him has an appointed term, so let her be patient and seek reward.” She sent to him, adjuring him to come to her. He rose, accompanied by Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah, Mu‘adh ibn Jabal, Ubayy ibn Ka‘b, Zayd ibn Thabit, and men. The boy was lifted up to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with his breath rattling.
He said: I think he said, “As though it were a worn waterskin.”

His eyes overflowed. Sa‘d said, “Messenger of Allah, what is this?” He said, “This is mercy that Allah has placed in the hearts of His servants. And Allah has mercy only on the merciful among His servants.”

arabic_blocks: [1225] حدثنا عبد الله بن محمد حدثنا أبو عامر حدثنا فليح بن سليمان عن هلال بن علي عن أنس بن مالك رضى الله تعالى عنه قال شهدنا بنتا لرسول الله ﷺ قال: ورسول الله ﷺ جالس على القبر قال: فرأيت عينيه تدمعان قال، فقال هل منكم رجل لم يقارف الليلة، فقال أبو طلحة أنا قال: فانزل قال: فنزل في قبرها
english_blocks: ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad related to us: Abu ‘Amir related to us: Fulayh ibn Sulayman related to us, from Hilal ibn ‘Ali, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

We attended a daughter of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was sitting by the grave. He said: I saw his eyes shedding tears. He said: Then he asked, “Is there a man among you who did not have intercourse last night?” Abu Talhah said, “I.” He said, “Then go down.” He said: He went down into her grave.

arabic_blocks: [1226] حدثنا عبدان حدثنا عبد الله أخبرنا ابن جريج قال: أخبرني عبد الله بن عبيد الله بن أبي مليكة قال توفيت ابنة لعثمان رضى الله تعالى عنه بمكة وجئنا لنشهدها وحضرها بن عمر وابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهم وإني لجالس بينهما أو قال جلست إلى أحدهما ثم جاء الآخر فجلس إلى جنبي، فقال عبد الله بن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما لعمرو بن عثمان ألا تنهى عن البكاء فأن رسول الله ﷺ قال: إن الميت ليعذب ببكاء أهله عليه، فقال ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما قد كان عمر رضى الله تعالى عنه يقول بعض ذلك ثم حدث قال صدرت مع عمر رضى الله تعالى عنه من مكة حتى إذا كنا بالبيداء إذا هو بركب تحت ظل سمرة، فقال اذهب فانظر من هؤلاء الركب قال: فنظرت فإذا صهيب فأخبرته، فقال ادعه لي فرجعت إلى صهيب فقلت: ارتحل فالحق أمير المؤمنين فلما أصيب عمر دخل صهيب يبكي يقول وا أخاه وا صاحباه، فقال عمر رضى الله تعالى عنه يا صهيب أتبكي علي وقد قال رسول الله ﷺ: إن الميت يعذب ببعض بكاء أهله عليه قال ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما فلما مات عمر رضى الله تعالى عنه ذكرت ذلك لعائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها فقالت رحم الله عمر والله ما حدث رسول الله ﷺ إن الله ليعذب المؤمن ببكاء أهله عليه ولكن رسول الله ﷺ قال: إن الله ليزيد الكافر عذابا ببكاء أهله عليه وقالت حسبكم القرآن { ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى } قال ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما عند ذلك والله { هو أضحك وأبكى } قال ابن أبي مليكة والله ما قال ابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما شيئا
english_blocks: ‘Abdan related to us: ‘Abd Allah related to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us; he said: ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah informed me; he said:

A daughter of ‘Uthman, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, died in Makkah, and we came to attend her. Ibn ‘Umar and Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them, were present, and I was sitting between them.
Or he said: “I sat beside one of them, then the other came and sat beside me.”

‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, said to ‘Amr ibn ‘Uthman, “Will you not forbid the weeping? For the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘The deceased is indeed punished because of his family’s weeping over him.’”

Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, said, “‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, used to say some of that.” Then he related, saying: “I departed from Makkah with ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with him. When we were at al-Bayda’, there was a party of riders in the shade of a samurah tree. He said, ‘Go and see who these riders are.’” He said: “I looked, and there was Suhayb. I informed him, and he said, ‘Call him to me.’ I returned to Suhayb and said, ‘Set out and join the Commander of the Believers.’ When ‘Umar was struck, Suhayb entered weeping, saying, ‘Alas, my brother! Alas, my companion!’ ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, said, ‘Suhayb, are you weeping over me when the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, has said, “The deceased is punished because of some of his family’s weeping over him”?’”

Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, said: When ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, died, I mentioned that to ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her. She said, “May Allah have mercy on ‘Umar. By Allah, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not state that Allah punishes the believer because of his family’s weeping over him. Rather, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Allah indeed increases the disbeliever’s punishment because of his family’s weeping over him.’” She said, “The Qur’an is sufficient for you: ‘No bearer of a burden bears the burden of another.’”
Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, said at that point, “By Allah, ‘He makes laugh and makes weep.’”
Ibn Abi Mulaykah said: By Allah, Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, said nothing.

arabic_blocks: [1227] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف أخبرنا مالك عن عبد الله بن أبي بكر عن أبيه عن عمرة بنت عبد الرحمن أنها أخبرته أنها سمعت عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها زوج النبي ﷺ قالت إنما مر رسول الله ﷺ على يهودية يبكي عليها أهلها، فقال إنهم ليبكون عليها وإنها لتعذب في قبرها
english_blocks: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us: Malik informed us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, from his father, from ‘Amrah bint ‘Abd al-Rahman, who informed him that she heard ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had only passed a Jewish woman whose family were weeping over her. He said, “They are indeed weeping over her, while she is being punished in her grave.”

english_blocks: Isma‘il ibn Khalil related to us: ‘Ali ibn Mus-hir related to us: Abu Ishaq—who is al-Shaybani—related to us, from Abu Burdah, from his father, who said:

english_blocks: Abu Nu‘aym related to us: Sa‘id ibn ‘Ubayd related to us, from ‘Ali ibn Rabi‘ah, from al-Mughirah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say, “A lie about me is not like a lie about anyone else. Whoever deliberately lies about me, let him take his seat in the Fire.” I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say, “Whoever is wailed over is punished because of the wailing over him.”

‘Abd al-A‘la corroborated him: Yazid ibn Zuray‘ related to us: Sa‘id related to us: Qatadah related to us.
And Adam said, from Shu‘bah: “The deceased is punished because of the living person’s weeping over him.”

arabic_blocks: [1231] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله حدثنا سفيان حدثنا ابن المنكدر قال: سمعت جابر بن عبد الله رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال جيء بأبي يوم أحد قد مثل به حتى وضع بين يدي رسول الله ﷺ وقد سجي ثوبا فذهبت أريد أن أكشف عنه فنهاني قومي ثم ذهبت أكشف عنه فنهاني قومي فأمر رسول الله ﷺ فرفع فسمع صوت صائحة، فقال من هذه فقالوا ابنة عمرو أو أخت عمرو قال: فلم تبكي أو لا تبكي فما زالت الملائكة تظله بأجنحتها حتى رفع
english_blocks: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us: Sufyan related to us: Ibn al-Munkadir related to us; he said: I heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, say:

My father was brought on the day of Uhud, having been mutilated, and was placed before the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, covered with a cloth. I went, intending to uncover him, but my people forbade me. Then I went to uncover him, but my people forbade me. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gave an order, and he was lifted away. He heard the voice of a woman crying out and said, “Who is this?” They said, “The daughter of ‘Amr—or the sister of ‘Amr.” He said, “Why is she weeping?”—or, “Let her not weep.”—“The angels continued to shade him with their wings until he was lifted away.”

english_blocks: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Amir ibn Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas, from his father, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to visit me in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage because of an illness that had become severe. I said, “The illness has brought me to this state. I have wealth, and only a daughter inherits from me. Shall I give two-thirds of my wealth in charity?” He said, “No.” I said, “Half?” He said, “No.” Then he said, “A third, and a third is great—or much. To leave your heirs wealthy is better than to leave them dependent, begging from people. You will not spend anything seeking thereby the Face of Allah without being rewarded for it, even what you put into your wife’s mouth.” I said, “Messenger of Allah, will I be left behind after my companions?” He said, “You will not be left behind and do a righteous deed without thereby increasing in degree and elevation. Then perhaps you will be left behind, so that some people benefit through you and others are harmed through you. Allah, complete my companions’ emigration for them, and do not turn them back on their heels. But poor Sa‘d ibn Khawlah!”
The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, grieved for him because he died in Makkah.

Abu Musa fell ill and fainted, with his head in the lap of a woman of his family, and he could not respond to her at all. When he recovered consciousness, he said, “I am free of those from whom the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, declared himself free. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, declared himself free of the woman who wails, the woman who shaves her hair, and the woman who tears her clothes.”

english_blocks: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us: ‘Abd al-Wahhab related to us; he said: I heard Yahya say: ‘Amrah informed me; she said: I heard ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, say:

When news of the killing of Ibn Harithah, Ja‘far and Ibn Rawahah reached the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he sat down with grief apparent in him, while I was looking through the opening of the door.
The crack in the door.

A man came to him and said, “The women of Ja‘far”—and he mentioned their weeping. He ordered him to forbid them. He went, then came to him a second time; they had not obeyed him. He said, “Forbid them.” He came to him a third time and said, “By Allah, they have overcome us, Messenger of Allah.”
She stated that he said:

“Then cast dust into their mouths.” I said, “May Allah rub your nose in the dust! You did not do what the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, commanded you, and you did not spare the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the trouble.”

english_blocks: Bishr ibn al-Hakam related to us: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah related to us: Ishaq ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah informed us that he heard Anas ibn Malik, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, say:

A son of Abu Talhah fell ill. He said: He died while Abu Talhah was away. When his wife saw that he had died, she prepared something and moved him to the side of the house. When Abu Talhah came, he asked, “How is the boy?” She said, “His soul has become still, and I hope he has found rest.” Abu Talhah thought that she was telling the truth. He said: He spent the night. When morning came, he bathed. When he intended to leave, she informed him that the boy had died. He prayed with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then informed the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, of what had happened between them. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Perhaps Allah will bless you both in your night.”
Sufyan said: A man of the Ansar then said, “I saw that they had nine children, all of whom had recited the Qur’an.”

We entered with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, upon Abu Sayf the blacksmith, who was the foster father of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, took Ibrahim, kissed him and smelled him. Then we entered upon him after that, while Ibrahim was breathing his last. The eyes of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, began to shed tears. ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, said to him, “Even you, Messenger of Allah?” He said, “Ibn ‘Awf, this is mercy.” Then he followed it with another, and said, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “The eye sheds tears and the heart grieves, and we say only what pleases our Lord. And we are indeed grieved by your departure, Ibrahim.”
Musa narrated it from Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah, from Thabit, from Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

arabic_blocks: [1242] حدثنا أصبغ عن ابن وهب قال: أخبرني عمرو عن سعيد بن الحارث الأنصارى عن عبد الله بن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال اشتكى سعد بن عبادة شكوى له فأتاه النبي ﷺ يعوده مع عبد الرحمن بن عوف وسعد بن أبي وقاص وعبد الله بن مسعود رضى الله تعالى عنهم فلما دخل عليه فوجده في غاشية أهله، فقال قد قضى قالوا لا يا رسول الله فبكى النبي ﷺ فلما رأى القوم بكاء النبي ﷺ بكوا، فقال ألا تسمعون إن الله لا يعذب بدمع العين ولا بحزن القلب ولكن يعذب بهذا وأشار إلى لسانه أو يرحم وإن الميت يعذب ببكاء أهله عليه
وكان عمر رضي الله عنه يضرب فيه بالعصا ويرمي بالحجارة ويحثي بالتراب
english_blocks: Asbagh related to us, from Ibn Wahb, who said: ‘Amr informed me, from Sa‘id ibn al-Harith al-Ansari, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah fell ill with an illness of his. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to visit him with ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf, Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas and ‘Abd Allah ibn Mas‘ud, may Allah Most High be pleased with them. When he entered upon him and found him surrounded by his family, he asked, “Has he passed away?” They said, “No, Messenger of Allah.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wept. When the people saw the weeping of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, they wept. He said, “Do you not hear? Allah does not punish because of the eye’s tears or the heart’s grief, but He punishes because of this”—
and he pointed to his tongue—
“or shows mercy. And the deceased is indeed punished because of his family’s weeping over him.”
And ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to strike with a stick because of it, throw stones, and scatter dust.

arabic_blocks: [1243] حدثنا محمد بن عبد الله بن حوشب حدثنا عبد الوهاب حدثنا يحيى بن سعيد قال: أخبرتني عمرة قالت سمعت عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها تقول لما جاء قتل زيد بن حارثة وجعفر وعبد الله بن رواحة جلس النبي ﷺ يعرف فيه الحزن وأنا أطلع من شق الباب فأتاه رجل، فقال: يا رسول الله إن نساء جعفر وذكر بكاءهن فأمره بأن ينهاهن فذهب الرجل ثم أتى، فقال قد نهيتهن وذكر أنهن لم يطعنه فأمره الثانية أن ينهاهن فذهب ثم أتى، فقال والله لقد غلبنني أو غلبننا الشك من محمد بن حوشب فزعمت أن النبي ﷺ قال: فاحث في أفواههن التراب فقلت: أرغم الله أنفك فوالله ما أنت بفاعل وما تركت رسول الله ﷺ من العناء
english_blocks: Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Hawshab related to us: ‘Abd al-Wahhab related to us: Yahya ibn Sa‘id related to us; he said: ‘Amrah informed me; she said: I heard ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, say:

When news of the killing of Zayd ibn Harithah, Ja‘far and ‘Abd Allah ibn Rawahah came, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sat down with grief apparent in him, while I was looking through the crack in the door. A man came to him and said, “Messenger of Allah, the women of Ja‘far”—and he mentioned their weeping. He ordered him to forbid them. The man went, then came and said, “I have forbidden them,” and mentioned that they had not obeyed him. He ordered him a second time to forbid them. He went, then came and said, “By Allah, they have indeed overcome me—or overcome us.”
The uncertainty is from Muhammad ibn Hawshab.
She stated that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Then cast dust into their mouths.” I said, “May Allah rub your nose in the dust! By Allah, you are not going to do it, and you have not spared the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the trouble.”

At the pledge of allegiance, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bound us not to wail. None of our women fulfilled it except five women: Umm Sulaym, Umm al-‘Ala’, the daughter of Abu Sabrah—Mu‘adh’s wife—and two women—or the daughter of Abu Sabrah and the wife of Mu‘adh and another woman.

english_blocks: Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us, from Sa‘id al-Maqburi, from his father, who said:

We were at a funeral. Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, took Marwan’s hand, and they sat down before it was put down. Abu Sa‘id, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, came and took Marwan’s hand, saying, “Stand up. By Allah, this man certainly knows that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade us from doing that.” Abu Hurayrah said, “He spoke the truth.”

arabic_blocks: [1250] حدثنا آدم حدثنا شعبة حدثنا عمرو بن مرة قال: سمعت عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى قال: كان سهل بن حنيف وقيس بن سعد قاعدين بالقادسية فمروا عليهما بجنازة فقاما فقيل لهما إنها من أهل الأرض أي من أهل الذمة فقالا إن النبي ﷺ مرت به جنازة فقام فقيل له إنها جنازة يهودي، فقال أليست نفسا، وقال أبو حمزة عن الأعمش عن عمرو عن ابن أبي ليلى قال: كنت مع قيس وسهل رضى الله تعالى عنهما فقالا كنا مع النبي ﷺ، وقال زكريا عن الشعبي عن ابن أبي ليلى كان أبو مسعود وقيس يقومان للجنازة
english_blocks: Adam related to us: Shu‘bah related to us: ‘Amr ibn Murrah related to us; he said: I heard ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla say:
Sahl ibn Hunayf and Qays ibn Sa‘d were sitting at al-Qadisiyyah. They passed them with a funeral procession, and the two stood. They were told, “It is one of the people of the land”—
that is, one of the people of the covenant of protection—
and the two said, “A funeral procession passed the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he stood. He was told, ‘It is the funeral of a Jew.’ He said, ‘Is it not a soul?’”

And Abu Hamzah said, from al-A‘mash, from ‘Amr, from Ibn Abi Layla, who said: I was with Qays and Sahl, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, and they said, “We were with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”
And Zakariyya said, from al-Sha‘bi, from Ibn Abi Layla: Abu Mas‘ud and Qays used to stand for the funeral procession.

english_blocks: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us: Al-Layth related to us, from Sa‘id al-Maqburi, from his father, that he heard Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When the servant is placed in his grave and his companions have turned away and departed, he even hears the sound of their sandals. Two angels come to him and make him sit up. He gives a cry that those near him hear, except humans and jinn.”

He returned to his Lord and said, “You sent me to a servant who does not want death.” Allah restored his eye and said, “Return and tell him to place his hand on the back of an ox. english_blocks: Isma‘il related to us; he said: Malik related to me, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was ill, some of his wives mentioned a church they had seen in the land of al-Habashah, called Mariyah. Umm Salamah and Umm Habibah, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, had been to the land of al-Habashah. They mentioned its beauty and pictures in it. He raised his head and said, “Those people, when a righteous man among them dies, build a place of worship over his grave, then make that image in it. Those are the worst of creation before Allah.”

english_blocks: Muhammad ibn Sinan related to us: Fulayh ibn Sulayman related to us: Hilal ibn ‘Ali related to us, from Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

We attended a daughter of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was sitting by the grave, and I saw his eyes shedding tears. He asked, “Is there anyone among you who did not have intercourse last night?” Abu Talhah said, “I.” He said, “Then go down into her grave.” He went down into her grave and buried her.
Ibn Mubarak said: Fulayh said, “I think he means sin.”
Abu ‘Abd Allah said: “That they may acquire”—that is, “that they may earn.”

english_blocks: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us: Al-Layth related to us; he said: Ibn Shihab related to me, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka‘b ibn Malik, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to bring together two of the men killed at Uhud in one garment. Then he would ask, “Which of them had learned more of the Qur’an?” When one of the two was pointed out to him, he placed him first in the side niche of the grave. He said, “I am a witness for these on the Day of Resurrection.” He ordered them to be buried in their blood. They were not washed, nor were they prayed over.

arabic_blocks: [1284] حدثنا محمد بن عبد الله بن حوشب حدثنا عبد الوهاب حدثنا خالد عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما عن النبي ﷺ قال: حرم الله مكة فلم تحل لأحد قبلي ولا لأحد بعدي أحلت لي ساعة من نهار لا يختلى خلاها ولا يعضد شجرها ولا ينفر صيدها ولا تلتقط لقطتها إلا لمعرف، فقال العباس رضى الله تعالى عنه إلا الإذخر لصاغتنا وقبورنا، فقال إلا الإذخر، وقال أبو هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه عن النبي ﷺ لقبورنا وبيوتنا، وقال أبان بن صالح عن الحسن بن مسلم عن صفية بنت شيبة سمعت النبي ﷺ مثله، وقال مجاهد عن طاوس عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما لقينهم وبيوتهم
english_blocks: Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Hawshab related to us: ‘Abd al-Wahhab related to us: Khalid related to us, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Allah made Makkah sacred. It was not made lawful for anyone before me or anyone after me. It was made lawful for me for a time during one day. Its fresh grass is not to be cut, its trees are not to be cut down, its game is not to be frightened away, and its lost property is not to be picked up except by one who makes it known.” Al-‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, said, “Except idhkhir, for our goldsmiths and our graves.” He said, “Except idhkhir.”
And Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, said, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “For our graves and our houses.”
And Aban ibn Salih said, from al-Hasan ibn Muslim, from Safiyyah bint Shaybah: I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say the same.
And Mujahid said, from Tawus, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, “For their smith and their houses.”

arabic_blocks: [1285] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله حدثنا سفيان قال عمرو سمعت جابر بن عبد الله رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال أتى رسول الله ﷺ عبد الله بن أبي بعد ما أدخل حفرته فأمر به فأخرج فوضعه على ركبتيه ونفث عليه من ريقه وألبسه قميصه فالله أعلم وكان كسا عباسا قميصا قال سفيان، وقال أبو هارون وكان على رسول الله ﷺ قميصان، فقال له بن عبد الله يا رسول الله ألبس أبي قميصك الذي يلي جلدك قال سفيان فيرون أن النبي ﷺ ألبس عبد الله قميصه مكافأة لما صنع
english_blocks: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us: Sufyan related to us. ‘Amr said: I heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, say:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy after he had been placed in his burial pit. He gave an order concerning him, and he was brought out. He placed him on his knees, blew lightly on him with some of his saliva and clothed him in his shirt.
Allah knows best.
He had clothed ‘Abbas in a shirt.

Sufyan said: And Abu Harun said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was wearing two shirts. The son of ‘Abd Allah said to him, “Messenger of Allah, clothe my father in the shirt of yours that is next to your skin.”
Sufyan said: They consider that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, clothed ‘Abd Allah in his shirt in return for what he had done.

arabic_blocks: [1286] حدثنا مسدد أخبرنا بشر بن المفضل حدثنا حسين المعلم عن عطاء عن جابر رضى الله تعالى عنه قال لما حضر أحد دعاني أبي من الليل، فقال: ما أراني إلا مقتولا في أول من يقتل من أصحاب النبي ﷺ وإني لا أترك بعدي أعز علي منك غير نفس رسول الله ﷺ فإن علي دينا فاقض واستوص بأخواتك خيرا فأصبحنا فكان أول قتيل ودفن معه آخر في قبر ثم لم تطب نفسي أن أتركه مع الآخر فاستخرجته بعد ستة أشهر فإذا هو كيوم وضعته هنية غير أذنه
english_blocks: Musaddad related to us: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal informed us: Husayn al-Mu‘allim related to us, from ‘Ata’, from Jabir, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

When Uhud approached, my father called me during the night and said, “I expect to be killed among the first of the companions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to be killed. I leave no one behind dearer to me than you, except the person of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. I have a debt, so pay it, and treat your sisters well.” When morning came, he was the first killed. Another was buried with him in a grave. Then I was not content to leave him with the other, so I took him out after six months. He was as he had been on the day I laid him there, except for a small change at his ear.

arabic_blocks: [1288] حدثنا عبدان أخبرنا عبد الله أخبرنا الليث بن سعد قال: حدثني ابن شهاب عن عبد الرحمن بن كعب بن مالك عن جابر بن عبد الله رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال: كان النبي ﷺ يجمع بين رجلين من قتلى أحد ثم يقول أيهم أكثر أخذا للقرآن فإذا أشير له إلى أحدهما قدمه في اللحد، فقال: أنا شهيد على هؤلاء يوم القيامة فأمر بدفنهم بدمائهم ولم يغسلهم
english_blocks: ‘Abdan related to us: ‘Abd Allah informed us: Al-Layth ibn Sa‘d informed us; he said: Ibn Shihab related to me, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka‘b ibn Malik, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to bring together two men killed at Uhud. Then he would ask, “Which of them had learned more of the Qur’an?” When one of the two was pointed out to him, he placed him first in the side niche of the grave. He said, “I am a witness for these on the Day of Resurrection.” He ordered them to be buried in their blood, and he did not wash them.
